sections.title: Mission · Open Source Has Licensing Rules
paragraphs: Open source is not simply software you do not have to pay for. Licensing determines what users and developers are legally permitted to do with software.
bullets: Free Software, Open Source Software, FOSS, and FLOSS
sections.callout: THE LICENSE DEFINES THE RIGHTS AND OBLIGATIONS

sections.title: Open Source Philosophy
paragraphs: Open-source software makes source code available under licensing terms that permit specified forms of inspection, modification, and redistribution. The exact rights and obligations depend on the license.
sections.callout: OPEN SOURCE DOES NOT MEAN NO RULES

sections.title: Free Software
paragraphs: Free Software emphasizes user freedoms. Free means freedom, not necessarily price. Software can be sold commercially and still be Free Software if its license provides the relevant freedoms.

sections.title: Open Source Software
paragraphs: Open Source Software emphasizes source code made available under an open-source license that permits specified use, modification, and redistribution. The Free Software and Open Source movements overlap heavily, although their philosophical emphasis can differ.
sections.callout: OPEN SOURCE = LICENSED RIGHTS TO USE, INSPECT, MODIFY, AND REDISTRIBUTE

sections.title: FOSS and FLOSS

entries.title: FLOSS
paragraphs: Free/Libre and Open Source Software. Libre clarifies that free refers to freedom rather than merely zero price.

sections.callout: FOSS = FREE + OPEN SOURCE · FLOSS = FREE/LIBRE + OPEN SOURCE

sections.title: Exam Trap — Free Software vs. Freeware
paragraphs: Do not assume free price means Free Software. Free Software refers to freedoms granted by licensing. A program costing $0 does not automatically satisfy Free Software or Open Source principles.
sections.callout: FREE PRICE IS NOT THE SAME AS SOFTWARE FREEDOM

sections.title: Free Software Foundation
paragraphs: The Free Software Foundation (FSF) promotes Free Software principles and user freedoms.

sections.title: Open Source Initiative
paragraphs: The Open Source Initiative (OSI) promotes and supports the open-source model and maintains the Open Source Definition and license-approval process.

sections.title: Copyleft
paragraphs: Copyleft licensing uses copyright law to preserve certain freedoms when software is redistributed or modified. Derivative or distributed versions may need to remain under corresponding licensing requirements.

sections.title: GNU General Public License
paragraphs: The GNU General Public License (GPL) is a major copyleft license.

entries.title: Scenario
paragraphs: A question emphasizes that redistributed derivative software must preserve GPL licensing obligations.

sections.title: Permissive Licenses
paragraphs: A permissive open-source license generally places fewer requirements on redistribution and reuse than strong copyleft licensing.

sections.title: BSD Licenses
paragraphs: BSD-style licenses are classic examples of permissive open-source licensing.

sections.title: Exam Trap — GPL vs. BSD

table.caption: Separate share-forward obligations from broader permission

sections.callout: GPL = GIVE FREEDOMS FORWARD · BSD = BROADER PERMISSION

sections.title: Creative Commons
paragraphs: Creative Commons licenses are commonly associated with creative works and content, including documentation, images, educational material, and media. Do not automatically treat Creative Commons as the normal software-code licensing answer.

sections.title: Open-Source Business Models
paragraphs: Open source does not prevent companies from making money. Organizations can build businesses around support, consulting, training, hosted services, enterprise features and services, integration, and maintenance.

entries.title: Scenario
paragraphs: A company distributes open-source software but charges customers for enterprise support. This can still be an open-source business model.
entries.recognitionCue: OPEN SOURCE DOES NOT MEAN NO BUSINESS

sections.title: GSA Scenario Recognition
bullets: Creative or media licensing → Creative Commons
Company sells support around open-source software → Open-source business model
sections.callout: Recognize the philosophy, organization, license model, license family, or business model.

sections.title: Maestro Recognition Sheet
bullets: Creative Commons → Creative works and content
FOSS → Free and Open Source Software
FLOSS → Free/Libre and Open Source Software
Open source → Licensed freedoms, not absence of copyright or rules
sections.callout: FSF = FREEDOM · OSI = OPEN SOURCE · GPL = COPYLEFT · BSD = PERMISSIVE · CC = CONTENT
